notes:
Lead origin: self-serve signup + inbound trial credit. Small B2B SaaS that ships an onboarding assistant and in-app help widget. Primary ask: hosted API (self-serve) with predictable behavior when traffic spikes (weekend promo, flash sales).

Summary of needs / pain:
- We hit 429s during internal load test (simulated promo spike ~120 concurrent sessions). Behavior was: sudden 429 cascade, client SDK retries aggressive -> doubled traffic, user-visible errors.
- Want per-key concurrency limits, clear retry headers (RFC-style Retry-After), and guidance on backoff to avoid retry storms.
- Cost-sensitive: wants burst handling without runaway token spend. Prefer short-term burst credits / token-bucket style allowances.
- Needs simple quota visibility in console or API (remaining quota, reset window) for self-serve customers.
- Prefers public cloud hosted offering; will likely stick to hosted API if controls reduce 429s and provide cost visibility.

Timeline (recent activity):
- 2025-01-10: Signup via website, used trial credits. AE (Jordan) auto-assigned.
- 2025-01-15: Initial discovery call (fireflies ff_20250122_8b9c2f). Collected latency/throughput targets.
- 2025-01-22: Internal load test (team): reproduced 429 cascade at ~120 concurrent sessions; recorded logs and thread (thread-CAJk3X9qL_2-peachgrove-demo).
- 2025-01-28: Sent security questionnaire; asked about SOC2 and audit log retention. Drive docs updated (security FAQ).
- 2025-02-03: Demo of hosted API and dashboard; showed per-key quotas but missing burst-credit concept. Follow-up requested.

Quoted from PoC lead: "We need graceful degradation — if the model is slammed, fall back to a smaller fast model or cached answer for known intents. Also, tell us how to show users a polite busy message rather than 500/429."

Technical constraints and targets:
- Workload: short chat turn (support triage), median response length 30-80 tokens.
- Latency target: p95 < 650ms for common flows.
- Throughput target: baseline 40 req/s, bursts to 200 req/s for a few minutes.
- Cost sensitivity: wants to cap spend per day and be alerted at 70% of that cap.

POC goals / success criteria:
- Validate that hosted API rate-limits are predictable and that headers convey remaining/quota/reset.
- Demonstrate a retry/backoff pattern that prevents amplification. Provide recommended SDK config.
- Show ability to route to cheaper model variant automatically when capacity constrained.
- Confirm console visibility for per-key usage and burst allowance.

Next steps (short):
- Jordan to enable a scoped POC key with configurable quotas and burst-limit (due 2025-02-07).
- SE (Priya) to provide sample client retry policy and SDK snippet; include guidance for exponential backoff + jitter.
- Technical doc: attach sample curl and JS retry loops; add monitoring dashboard link.

Current sentiment: curious but cautious — will move fast if POC proves 429s handled gracefully and cost can be bounded.
